parts.text: What other organism is usually associated with this?

parts_raw.text: What other organism is usually associated with this?

questions.model_answer: a) Enterobius vermicularis (pinworm) — Dientamoeba fragilis is thought to be co-transmitted within Enterobius eggs, and the two are frequently found together.

questions.question: For the following parasites, indicate whether treatment is indicated and, if yes, indicate what the treatment is.
questions.question_raw: For the following parasites, indicate if a treatment is indicated and if yes indicate what is the treatment.
questions.model_answer:
a) Strongyloides (stercoralis): Yes — treat all infections (risk of hyperinfection). Ivermectin 200 mcg/kg daily for 2 days is first line. Exclude concurrent Loa loa before ivermectin in patients with relevant exposure, given risk of encephalopathy with high microfilarial loads.
b) Entamoeba hartmanni: No — nonpathogenic commensal; no treatment indicated.
c) Blastocystis hominis: No (generally) — usually nonpathogenic; treat only if symptomatic and other causes excluded, with metronidazole (or TMP-SMX/nitazoxanide).
d) Trichuris trichiura: Yes (if symptomatic/heavy burden) — albendazole or mebendazole; can cause dysentery, anemia, and rectal prolapse/proctitis in heavy infection.
questions.beyond_mandell: Not covered by the supplied mycetoma chapter text; answer based on established Mandell intestinal-parasite chapters and standard treatment guidance.

cohort_answer.text:
Strongyloides: Yes – Ivermectin. Test for Loa-loa, can get encephalopathy if treated with ivermectin (daytime blood smear for microfilaria)
Entameoba hartmanii: No
B. hominis: No
Trichuris trichuria: Yes – Mebendazole
- can cause dysentery, anaemia and proctitis

questions.question: Identify the following stool parasites to genus and species level from the micrographs shown.
questions.question_raw: 49. Identify the following stool parasites to genus and species level (see pictures)

parts.text: [image-based question: micrograph, Hematoxylin and eosin stain] Identify to genus and species level.
[image-based question: micrograph, Modified acid fast stain (Kinyoun) with ruler indicating 6 micrometers] Identify to genus and species level.
[image-based question: micrograph, Hematoxylin and eosin stain] Identify to genus and species level.

parts_raw.text: [image-based question: micrograph, Hematoxylin and eosin stain] Identify to genus and species level
a) [image-based question: micrograph, Modified acid fast stain (Kinyoun) with ruler indicating 6 micrometers] Identify to genus and species level
c) [image-based question: micrograph, Hematoxylin and eosin stain] Identify to genus and species level

questions.model_answer:
a) Entamoeba histolytica. Trophozoite with a single nucleus bearing a small central karyosome and fine, evenly distributed peripheral chromatin; presence of ingested erythrocytes (erythrophagocytosis) is characteristic and distinguishes it from the morphologically identical non-pathogenic E. dispar.
b) Cryptosporidium parvum (C. hominis is morphologically identical). Modified acid-fast (Kinyoun) stain shows round oocysts ~4-6 micrometers (fitting the 6-micrometer ruler) that stain bright pink/red against a blue-green background, often with variable staining and internal sporozoites. Size distinguishes it from Cyclospora cayetanensis (8-10 micrometers) and Cystoisospora belli (elongated, ~20-30 micrometers).
c) Giardia duodenalis (lamblia). Pear/teardrop-shaped trophozoite with two nuclei giving the classic "owl's-face" appearance, or an oval four-nucleate cyst.
questions.beyond_mandell: Chapter 271 (p. 3271) names these organisms as intestinal protozoa but gives no diagnostic morphology; species-level microscopic identification is from the organism-specific Mandell chapters and CDC DPDx.

cohort_answer.text: First H&E image: E. histolytica (E. histolytica may be observed with ingested red blood cells/erythrophagocytosis; E. dispar may occasionally show ingested erythrocytes but to a much lesser degree). Modified acid fast (Kinyoun): Cryptosporidium parvum - oocysts rounded, 4.2-5.4 micrometers diameter, sporozoites sometimes visible indicating sporulation; stained bright red against blue-green background. Second H&E image (c): Giardia lamblia.

questions.question: For a stool report showing Strongyloides, Entamoeba hartmanni, Blastocystis, and Trichuris, indicate whether you would treat each and with what.

parts.text: For Strongyloides, Entamoeba hartmanni, Blastocystis, and Trichuris, state whether you would treat and with what.

parts_raw.text: Strongyloides, E hartmanni, blasto, trichuris Q - would you treat and with what?

questions.model_answer: a) (1) Strongyloides stercoralis - TREAT: ivermectin 200 µg/kg daily x2 days (lifelong autoinfection and risk of hyperinfection make eradication essential). (2) Entamoeba hartmanni - DO NOT treat: non-pathogenic commensal amoeba. (3) Blastocystis (hominis) - generally DO NOT treat in an asymptomatic patient; pathogenicity is uncertain. (4) Trichuris trichiura - TREAT: albendazole 400 mg PO x3-7 days (or mebendazole).
questions.beyond_mandell: Entamoeba hartmanni and Blastocystis are not intestinal nematodes; the decision not to treat these non-/uncertain pathogens follows standard parasitology (Mandell protozoa chapters/CDC).
